proof:
Source: parent-supplied proof of coarea_normDet_chain_rule, step 5 (block form of A). There, normDet(A) = |det A₁₁|·|det A_K| with A₁₁ = p_W ∘ A|_{K^⊥} and A_K = A|_K, and |det A_K| = normDet(A ∘ ι_K) by step 1(i). Here A : ℝⁿ → T is replaced by an arbitrary bijective f : V → X.
Notation: F := f(K) ⊆ X (Lean K.map f), so W = F^⊥. f_K : K → F is f_K(k) := f(k). g := p_W ∘ f ∘ ι_{K^⊥} : K^⊥ → W.

1. (Dimensions.) Put r := dim K and s := dim K^⊥; then r + s = dim V (Submodule.finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal). Since f is bijective, dim X = dim V (LinearEquiv.ofBijective). Since f is injective, it maps K isomorphically onto F (Submodule.equivMapOfInjective), so dim F = r. Since W = F^⊥, dim F + dim W = dim X, hence dim W = s.

2. (Orthonormal bases of the four pieces.) Choose orthonormal bases b₁ = (b₁,i)_{i<r} of K, b₂ = (b₂,j)_{j<s} of K^⊥, c₁ = (c₁,i)_{i<r} of F and c₂ = (c₂,j)_{j<s} of W. For example, take stdOrthonormalBasis and reindex along dim F = r and dim W = s from step 1.

3. (Adapted bases of V and X with a common index set.)
- V is the orthogonal direct sum K ⊕ K^⊥. So the family β indexed by Fin r ⊕ Fin s with β(inl i) = b₁,i and β(inr j) = b₂,j is an orthonormal basis of V. In Lean: (b₁.prod b₂).map K.orthogonalDecomposition.symm, using OrthonormalBasis.prod and Submodule.orthogonalDecomposition; the values follow from OrthonormalBasis.prod_apply and Submodule.orthogonalDecomposition_symm_apply.
- Likewise X = F ⊕ F^⊥ = F ⊕ W orthogonally. So γ with γ(inl i) = c₁,i and γ(inr j) = c₂,j is an orthonormal basis of X. In Lean: (c₁.prod c₂').map F.orthogonalDecomposition.symm, where c₂' is c₂ transported along W = F^⊥ by LinearIsometryEquiv.ofEq.

4. (The matrix of f is block upper triangular.) Let M be the matrix of f in the bases β, γ. Coordinates in an orthonormal basis are inner products, so M_{a,b} = ⟨γ(a), f(β(b))⟩ (LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, OrthonormalBasis.repr_apply_apply).
(a) a = inl i, b = inl j: M_{a,b} = ⟨c₁,i, f(b₁,j)⟩ = ⟨c₁,i, f_K(b₁,j)⟩_F, because the inner product of F is the restriction of that of X. This is the (i,j) entry of the matrix M₁₁ of f_K in the bases b₁, c₁.
(b) a = inr i, b = inl j: c₂,i ∈ W = F^⊥ and f(b₁,j) ∈ f(K) = F, so M_{a,b} = 0 (Submodule.inner_left_of_mem_orthogonal).
(c) a = inr i, b = inr j: for w ∈ W and x ∈ X, ⟨w, x⟩ = ⟨w, p_W x⟩, since x − p_W x ⊥ W (Submodule.inner_orthogonalProjectionOnto_eq_of_mem_left). Hence M_{a,b} = ⟨c₂,i, p_W(f(b₂,j))⟩_W = ⟨c₂,i, g(b₂,j)⟩_W, the (i,j) entry of the matrix M₂₂ of g in the bases b₂, c₂.
(d) a = inl i, b = inr j: M_{a,b} = ⟨c₁,i, f(b₂,j)⟩ =: M₁₂(i,j), which is unconstrained.
Therefore M = [[M₁₁, M₁₂], [0, M₂₂]], i.e. Matrix.fromBlocks M₁₁ M₁₂ 0 M₂₂.

5. (Determinant.) det M = det M₁₁ · det M₂₂ (Matrix.det_fromBlocks_zero₂₁). When r = 0 or s = 0, the empty block has determinant 1 and the formula still holds.

6. (normDet as |det| in square orthonormal bases.) When both orthonormal bases share a finite index set, normDet is |det| of the matrix (LinearMap.normDet_eq_norm_det_toMatrix). Thus normDet f = |det M|, normDet f_K = |det M₁₁| and normDet g = |det M₂₂|.

7. (f ∘ ι_K versus f_K.) f ∘ ι_K = ι_F ∘ f_K; that is, f_K is the codomain restriction of f ∘ ι_K to F. So normDet(f ∘ ι_K) = normDet(f_K) (LinearMap.normDet_codRestrict).

8. (Conclusion.) normDet f = |det M₁₁|·|det M₂₂| = normDet(f ∘ ι_K)·normDet(p_W ∘ f ∘ ι_{K^⊥}). ∎

This argument was checked in Lean in a scratch file; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
key_steps: dim f(K) = dim K and dim W = dim K^⊥, because f is bijective and W = f(K)^⊥.
Build orthonormal bases of V adapted to K ⊕ K^⊥ and of X adapted to f(K) ⊕ W, both indexed by Fin r ⊕ Fin s (OrthonormalBasis.prod with orthogonalDecomposition).
The matrix of f is fromBlocks M₁₁ M₁₂ 0 M₂₂: M₁₁ is the matrix of f|_K : K → f(K) and M₂₂ that of p_W∘f∘ι_{K^⊥}, since W ⊥ f(K) and ⟨w,x⟩ = ⟨w,p_W x⟩ for w ∈ W.
det M = det M₁₁·det M₂₂, normDet = |det| in square orthonormal bases, and normDet_codRestrict gives normDet(f|_K) = normDet(f∘ι_K).
